input.quote: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only Customer's payment obligations; searches for "transition", "return", "export" and "delet" show no exit assistance, data return/export or deletion obligations anywhere in this hosting agreement (14.18 Data Protection covers only contact information, and 11.6 makes Customer responsible for Content without any return mechanic). With no obligation to return Content, this falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export), so we insert the preferred exit clause into § 3.5, which is already carried forward by the § 14.2 survival list.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, IBM shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Content in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Content from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard exit clause to Section 3.5 so that, on termination, IBM provides up to six months of paid transition assistance and returns our Content in a machine-readable format within 30 days before deleting it and certifying deletion. The Agreement is currently silent on data return and wind-down, which would leave our hosted data stranded; we can accept a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and Content return/deletion obligation in § 3.5.
